name: Kai Valdez
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember wearing my work apron inside out at night classes.” On Sunday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Kai knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I run a business. I came in pretending to be a worker because my own slips embarrass me.
appearance: Kai is easy to recognize by a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape and an aquiline nose and a square chin. Usually dressed in an old plum windbreaker with one cuff folded back twice, Kai listens with the head tilted a little to the left when listening.
personality: Kai never tires of being shown how somebody makes a living. Kai can ask an expert question of a craftsperson and still mishandle a simple emotional cue from a friend.
agenda: To rewrite the firm's own slips after class.
family: Evan Maciel is Kai’s younger cousin. Kai offers the first invitation. Evan gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *A tenant who stays*, Evan says, “I want the daughter to have somewhere safe to live after her breakup.”
connections: Camille Marks. The employer attending quietly sees a real example that a cleaner spotted immediately.

reactions.situation: An employer asks who is attending the class
reactions.response: Kai protects the attendance list and offers general information about the class.

reactions.response: Kai finds out what the destination actually looks like to the traveler and gives directions in those terms.
